text.p: Italian bonds and bond futures pulled themselves up in late trade amid market relief that comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan did not upset U.S. markets.

The March LIFFE future was 26 basis points up at 131.74 while the July 2006 Btp was 21 basis points higher at 110.89 yielding 7.26 percent and with a 151 basis point spread over the benchmark 10-year Bund. The lira held around the 971 per mark area, helped by dollar steadiness.
The market was waiting for nine sample Italian cities' data due after 1630 GMT on January inflation prices.

Two cities' figures yesterday gave a preliminary year on year rate of 2.5-2.6 percent and 0.1 percent month on month, compared with December's final 2.6 percent and 0.1 percent month on month rate. Confirmation of those rates would encourage the market, although traders note that due to little progress in a long-running metal workers and employers wage dispute, an official Italian interest rate cut is unlikely just yet.

Traders say once Btp futures get to the 132.00 area they could be close to the top of their run for now. "I wouldn't like to be buying it there," one said. However others note every time there is a sell off buyers come back again.--Milan +392 66129507
